SLOOS-informed adjustment:
- The Fed’s highly accommodative stance (0–0.25 percent policy rate, average-inflation-targeting framework, and ongoing Treasury/agency MBS purchases) remains consistent with improved market functioning and supportive mortgage financing conditions noted in both the FOMC statement and recent surveys.
- However, SLOOS responses indicate that bank lending practices were influenced by capital and risk-management considerations and by forbearance policies, tempering the pass-through of accommodation to parts of the real economy. Banks reported stronger demand in safer mortgage segments—especially GSE-eligible and QM non-jumbo mortgages, which make up a large share of originations—while demand was weaker in subprime mortgage segments. This divergence suggests credit is flowing more smoothly to higher-quality borrowers than to riskier households and businesses.
- Taken together, the supportive stance and improved functioning in Treasuries and agency MBS are positives, but the bank credit channel remains uneven, with comparatively weaker appetite and availability for riskier credit. That skews risks modestly to the downside relative to an FSR-only read, though still mitigated by policy backstops.

Net tone: slightly negative, edged down by SLOOS evidence of uneven credit demand/availability outside conforming mortgages.
